answer.rationale: The write-path p99 began climbing shortly after a release went out 2 hours ago, so the release is the leading causal hypothesis and rollback is the only candidate that addresses cause rather than symptom. memory_b2 explicitly rules out regional_failover here: it restored latency fast but opened a 40-minute replication gap and lost writes, with a standing instruction never to fail over while writes are hot — and writes are at daily peak, which is exactly the excluded condition. route_read_replicas (b5) helped a read-driven dashboard load problem, not a write-path regression, so it is likely off-target; add_capacity (b3) was pre-provisioned headroom ahead of a known peak, not a mid-incident remedy, and would take effect too slowly; circuit breakers (b4) contained an external partner outage, and there is no evidence of a dependency failure here, so tripping one would shed our own healthy traffic. I want to verify b1 because it is the compressed basis for my chosen action: 'no customer impact' may have been recorded under low write volume or with a rollback-safe build, and if the day-18 rollback did not involve hot writes or schema/data migrations, its reassurance does not transfer to day 74. I want to verify b6 because it determines whether the release infrastructure supports staged/canary cohorts — if so I can roll back one cohort first, get a causal read inside an hour as b6 reports, and avoid a fleet-wide change during peak settlement. Downstream value risk: if the 2-hour-old release included a forward-only migration, rolling back could make in-flight settlement writes unreadable or dropped, which violates the primary objective more severely than the latency itself; the guarded cohort is chosen specifically to expose that before it is broad. I am not confident the release is the cause — 90 minutes of climb against a 2-hour-old release is consistent but could also be peak-load saturation coinciding with the deploy, and the guarded scale preserves that uncertainty rather than resolving it by assertion.
